title: Motion in a Plane and Vectors
syllabus: Scalars and Vectors, Vector addition and subtraction, Scalar and vector products, Unit vector, Resolution of a vector, Relative velocity, Motion in a plane, Projectile motion, Uniform circular motion

questions.question: A bullet is fired from a gun at the speed of $280\text{ m/s}$ in the direction $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. The maximum height attained by the bullet is: (Take $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2, \sin 30^\circ = 0.5$) (NEET 2023)
questions.solution: Maximum height $H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} = \frac{(280)^2 \times (0.5)^2}{2 \times 9.8} = \frac{78400 \times 0.25}{19.6} = \frac{19600}{19.6} = 1000\text{ m}$.

questions.question: A ball is projected from point $A$ with velocity $20\text{ m/s}$ at an angle $60^\circ$ to the horizontal direction. At the highest point of the path, the velocity of the ball will be: (NEET 2023)
questions.solution: At the highest point, vertical component of velocity becomes zero ($v_y = 0$) and horizontal component remains constant: $v = u_x = u\cos\theta = 20\cos 60^\circ = 20 \times 0.5 = 10\text{ m/s}$.

questions.question: A ball is projected with a velocity of $10\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $60^\circ$ with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be: (NEET 2022)
questions.solution:
Angle with horizontal is $\theta = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.
Speed at highest point $= u\cos\theta = 10\cos 30^\circ = 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 5\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}$.

questions.question: A cricket ball is thrown by a player at a speed of $20\text{ m/s}$ in a direction $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. The maximum height attained by the ball during its motion is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$) (NEET 2022)
questions.solution: $H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} = \frac{(20)^2 \sin^2 30^\circ}{2 \times 10} = \frac{400 \times (1/4)}{20} = \frac{100}{20} = 5\text{ m}$.

questions.question: A particle moving in a circle of radius $R$ with a uniform speed takes a time $T$ to complete one revolution. If this particle were projected with the same speed at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it equals $4R$. The angle of projection $\theta$ is then given by: (NEET 2021)
questions.solution:
Speed in circular motion: $v = \frac{2\pi R}{T}$.
Maximum height: $H = \frac{v^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} = 4R$.
$$\frac{\left(\frac{2\pi R}{T}\right)^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} = 4R \implies \frac{4\pi^2 R^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g T^2} = 4R$$
$$\sin^2\theta = \frac{2g T^2}{\pi^2 R} \implies \theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2gT^2}{\pi^2 R}\right)^{1/2}$$

questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates at $5\text{ m/s}^2$. At $t = 4\text{ s}$, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at $t = 6\text{ s}$? (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$) (NEET 2021)
questions.solution:
At $t = 4\text{ s}$, horizontal velocity of car $v_x = at = 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ m/s}$.
After release, horizontal velocity remains constant: $v_x = 20\text{ m/s}$.
Time elapsed in air $\Delta t = 6 - 4 = 2\text{ s}$.
Vertical velocity $v_y = g \Delta t = 10 \times 2 = 20\text{ m/s}$.
Resultant speed $v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(20)^2 + (20)^2} = 20\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$.
Once dropped, the only acceleration acting on the ball is gravity: $a = g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$ downward.

questions.question: A particle moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ is acted upon by three forces shown by the vector triangle $PQR$ in cyclic order. The velocity of the particle will: (NEET 2019)
questions.solution: Vectors representing the three forces form a closed cyclic triangle, so $\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = \vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2 + \vec{F}_3 = \vec{0}$. Since net force is zero, acceleration is zero and the velocity remains constant.

questions.question: The $x$ and $y$ coordinates of a particle at any time are $x = 5t - 2t^2$ and $y = 10t$ respectively, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres and $t$ in seconds. The acceleration of the particle at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is: (NEET 2017)
questions.solution:
$v_x = \frac{dx}{dt} = 5 - 4t \implies a_x = \frac{dv_x}{dt} = -4\text{ m/s}^2$.
$v_y = \frac{dy}{dt} = 10 \implies a_y = \frac{dv_y}{dt} = 0$.
Total acceleration $\vec{a} = a_x\hat{i} + a_y\hat{j} = -4\hat{i}\text{ m/s}^2$. Its magnitude is $-4\text{ m/s}^2$ along the x-direction.

questions.question: If the magnitude of sum of two vectors is equal to the magnitude of difference of the two vectors, the angle between these vectors is: (NEET 2016)
questions.solution:
$|\vec{A} + \vec{B}| = |\vec{A} - \vec{B}|$
$$A^2 + B^2 + 2AB\cos\theta = A^2 + B^2 - 2AB\cos\theta$$
$$4AB\cos\theta = 0 \implies \cos\theta = 0 \implies \theta = 90^\circ$$

questions.question: A particle moves so that its position vector is given by $\vec{r} = \cos\omega t\,\hat{x} + \sin\omega t\,\hat{y}$, where $\omega$ is a constant. Which of the following is true? (NEET 2016)
options: Velocity is perpendicular to $\vec{r}$ and acceleration is directed towards origin
Velocity and acceleration are both perpendicular to $\vec{r}$
Velocity and acceleration are both parallel to $\vec{r}$
Velocity is directed towards the origin and acceleration is perpendicular to $\vec{r}$
questions.solution:
$\vec{v} = \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = -\omega\sin\omega t\,\hat{x} + \omega\cos\omega t\,\hat{y}$.
$\vec{v} \cdot \vec{r} = -\omega\sin\omega t\cos\omega t + \omega\cos\omega t\sin\omega t = 0 \implies \vec{v} \perp \vec{r}$.
$\vec{a} = \frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = -\omega^2(\cos\omega t\,\hat{x} + \sin\omega t\,\hat{y}) = -\omega^2\vec{r}$.
Thus, acceleration is directed opposite to $\vec{r}$ (towards the origin).

questions.question: Two projectiles of same mass and with same initial velocity are thrown at an angle $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ with the horizontal. Which of the following will be the same for both projectiles?
questions.solution:
Horizontal range is $R = \frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$.
For complementary angles $(\theta_1 + \theta_2 = 60^\circ + 30^\circ = 90^\circ)$, $\sin(2 \times 60^\circ) = \sin 120^\circ = \sin 60^\circ = \sin(2 \times 30^\circ)$. Thus, horizontal range is identical.

questions.question: A unit vector is represented by $a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + c\hat{k}$. If $a = 0.6$ and $b = 0.8$, the value of $c$ must be:
questions.solution:
For a unit vector, $|\hat{u}| = 1 \implies a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 1$.
$$(0.6)^2 + (0.8)^2 + c^2 = 1 \implies 0.36 + 0.64 + c^2 = 1 \implies 1.0 + c^2 = 1 \implies c = 0$$

questions.question: Two vectors $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}$ and $\vec{B} = 4\hat{j} - 4\hat{i} + \alpha\hat{k}$ are perpendicular to each other. The value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.solution:
For perpendicular vectors, $\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = 0$.
$$\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = (2)(-4) + (3)(4) + (8)(\alpha) = 0$$
$$-8 + 12 + 8\alpha = 0 \implies 4 + 8\alpha = 0 \implies \alpha = -\frac{4}{8} = -\frac{1}{2}$$

questions.question: The angle between vectors $(\vec{A} \times \vec{B})$ and $(\vec{B} \times \vec{A})$ is:
questions.solution: Since cross product is anti-commutative, $(\vec{B} \times \vec{A}) = -(\vec{A} \times \vec{B})$. The two vectors are equal in magnitude but point in exactly opposite directions, making the angle between them $\pi\text{ radian}$ ($180^\circ$).

questions.question: If $|\vec{A} \times \vec{B}| = \sqrt{3}\,(\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B})$, then the magnitude of $(\vec{A} + \vec{B})$ is:
questions.solution:
$AB\sin\theta = \sqrt{3} AB\cos\theta \implies \tan\theta = \sqrt{3} \implies \theta = 60^\circ$.
$$|\vec{A} + \vec{B}| = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2 + 2AB\cos 60^\circ} = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2 + 2AB(1/2)} = (A^2 + B^2 + AB)^{1/2}$$

questions.question: A particle moves in $x\text{-}y$ plane according to the rule $x = a\sin\omega t$ and $y = a\cos\omega t$. The path of the particle is:
questions.solution: $x^2 + y^2 = a^2\sin^2\omega t + a^2\cos^2\omega t = a^2(\sin^2\omega t + \cos^2\omega t) = a^2$, which represents the equation of a circle of radius $a$.

questions.question: The linear velocity of a rotating body is given by $\vec{v} = \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}$. If $\vec{\omega} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{r} = 4\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$, then the magnitude of $\vec{v}$ is:
A boat crosses a river of width $1\text{ km}$ along the shortest possible path in $15\text{ minutes}$. If the speed of the river stream is $3\text{ km/h}$, the speed of the boat in still water is:
questions.solution:
For shortest path (straight across), resultant velocity $v_R = \frac{\text{width}}{\text{time}} = \frac{1\text{ km}}{15/60\text{ h}} = 4\text{ km/h}$.
Since $v_R = \sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2} \implies 4 = \sqrt{v_b^2 - 3^2} \implies v_b^2 = 16 + 9 = 25 \implies v_b = 5\text{ km/h}$.

questions.question: A person aiming to reach the exactly opposite point on the bank of a stream is swimming at a speed of $0.5\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $120^\circ$ with the direction of flow of water. The speed of water in the stream is:
questions.solution:
Angle with downstream is $120^\circ$, so angle with upstream/normal is $\theta = 120^\circ - 90^\circ = 30^\circ$.
To cancel drift: $v_r = v_m \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \times \frac{1}{2} = 0.25\text{ m/s}$.

questions.question: Rain is falling vertically downwards with a speed of $35\text{ m/s}$. A woman rides a bicycle with a speed of $12\text{ m/s}$ in east to west direction. What is the direction in which she should hold her umbrella to protect herself from rain?
questions.solution:
Relative velocity of rain with respect to woman: $\vec{v}_{rw} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_w = -35\hat{j} - (-12\hat{i}) = 12\hat{i} - 35\hat{j}$.
She must hold umbrella in opposite direction to relative velocity, making angle $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v_w}{v_r}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{35}\right)$ with the vertical towards the West.

questions.question: The equation of trajectory of a projectile is given by $y = \sqrt{3}x - \frac{g x^2}{2}$. The angle of projection with the horizontal is:
questions.solution:
Comparing with $y = x\tan\theta - \frac{g x^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$:
$\tan\theta = \sqrt{3} \implies \theta = 60^\circ$.

questions.question: For a projectile, the ratio of maximum height $H$ to the square of time of flight $T^2$ is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
$H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$ and $T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g} \implies T^2 = \frac{4u^2 \sin^2\theta}{g^2}$.
$$\frac{H}{T^2} = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta / 2g}{4u^2 \sin^2\theta / g^2} = \frac{g}{8} = \frac{10}{8} = \frac{5}{4}$$

questions.question: A projectile is thrown with an initial velocity $\vec{u} = a\hat{i} + b\hat{j}$. If the range of the projectile is equal to twice the maximum height, then:
questions.solution:
Range $R = \frac{2 u_x u_y}{g} = \frac{2ab}{g}$. Maximum height $H = \frac{u_y^2}{2g} = \frac{b^2}{2g}$.
Given $R = 2H \implies \frac{2ab}{g} = 2\left(\frac{b^2}{2g}\right) = \frac{b^2}{g} \implies 2ab = b^2 \implies b = 2a$ (or $\tan\theta = 2$). For $R = 4H \implies b=a$; here $R=2H \implies b=2a$.

questions.question: The angular speed of the minute hand of a clock in $\text{rad/s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Minute hand completes 1 rotation ($2\pi\text{ rad}$) in $60\text{ minutes} = 3600\text{ seconds}$.
$$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{3600} = \frac{\pi}{1800}\text{ rad/s}$$

questions.question: A particle moves along a circular path of radius $r$ with uniform angular velocity $\omega$. Its centripetal acceleration is:
questions.solution: For uniform circular motion, the acceleration is purely centripetal with magnitude $a_c = \omega^2 r = \frac{v^2}{r}$, pointing radially inwards towards the center.

questions.question: A body executes uniform circular motion in a horizontal plane. Which of the following physical quantities remains CONSTANT during the motion?
questions.solution: In uniform circular motion, speed $v$ is constant. Kinetic energy $K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ is a scalar and depends only on speed, hence remains constant. Velocity, acceleration, and momentum are vectors and constantly change direction.

questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$ with constant speed and time period $0.2\pi\text{ s}$. The acceleration of the particle is:
questions.solution:
$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2\pi}{0.2\pi} = 10\text{ rad/s}$.
Radius $r = 5\text{ cm} = 0.05\text{ m}$.
$$a = \omega^2 r = (10)^2 \times 0.05 = 100 \times 0.05 = 5\text{ m/s}^2$$

questions.question: Two vectors of equal magnitude $P$ have a resultant of magnitude $P$. The angle between the two vectors is:
questions.solution: $R = 2P\cos(\theta/2) \implies P = 2P\cos(\theta/2) \implies \cos(\theta/2) = 1/2 \implies \theta/2 = 60^\circ \implies \theta = 120^\circ$.

questions.question: The area of a parallelogram whose adjacent sides are determined by the vectors $\vec{a} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - 7\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -7 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(-1 + 21) - \hat{j}(1 - 6) + \hat{k}(-7 + 2) = 20\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$$
$$\text{Area} = |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = \sqrt{(20)^2 + 5^2 + (-5)^2} = \sqrt{400 + 25 + 25} = \sqrt{450} = 15\sqrt{2}$$

questions.question: A vector $\vec{A}$ makes angles $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with the x-axis and y-axis respectively. The angle it makes with the z-axis is:
questions.solution:
Direction cosines satisfy $\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1$.
$$\cos^2(30^\circ) + \cos^2(60^\circ) + \cos^2\gamma = 1 \implies \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \cos^2\gamma = 1$$
$$\frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{4} + \cos^2\gamma = 1 \implies 1 + \cos^2\gamma = 1 \implies \cos\gamma = 0 \implies \gamma = 90^\circ$$

questions.question: A body is projected with kinetic energy $K$ at an angle of $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. Its kinetic energy at the highest point of its trajectory is:
questions.solution:
Speed at highest point is $v = u\cos 45^\circ = \frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}$.
$$K' = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = \frac{1}{2}m \left(\frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}mu^2\right) = \frac{K}{2}$$

questions.question: The speed of a projectile at its maximum height is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ times its initial speed. The horizontal range of the projectile is:
questions.solution:
$u\cos\theta = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} u \implies \cos\theta = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \implies \theta = 30^\circ$.
$$R = \frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g} = \frac{u^2 \sin 60^\circ}{g} = \frac{\sqrt{3} u^2}{2g}$$

questions.question: Two cars $A$ and $B$ are travelling in the same direction with velocities $v_A = 80\text{ km/h}$ and $v_B = 60\text{ km/h}$. The relative velocity of car $A$ with respect to car $B$ is:
options: $20\text{ km/h}$ in direction of motion of car $A$
$140\text{ km/h}$ in direction of motion of car $A$
questions.solution: $\vec{v}_{AB} = \vec{v}_A - \vec{v}_B = 80 - 60 = +20\text{ km/h}$ along the direction of motion of car $A$.

questions.question: A body is projected horizontally from the top of a tower of height $80\text{ m}$ with a velocity of $20\text{ m/s}$. The horizontal distance from the foot of tower where the body hits the ground is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
Time to fall: $t = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 80}{10}} = \sqrt{16} = 4\text{ s}$.
Horizontal range: $x = u_x t = 20 \times 4 = 80\text{ m}$.

questions.question: The horizontal range and maximum height of a projectile are equal when the angle of projection is:
questions.solution:
Relation between $R$ and $H$: $R = 4H\cot\theta \implies \frac{R}{H} = \frac{4}{\tan\theta}$.
Given $R = H \implies \tan\theta = 4 \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}(4)$.

questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius $r = 2\text{ m}$ with a constant tangential speed of $4\text{ m/s}$. The net acceleration of the particle is:
questions.solution:
Since speed is constant, tangential acceleration $a_t = 0$.
Centripetal acceleration $a_c = \frac{v^2}{r} = \frac{4^2}{2} = \frac{16}{2} = 8\text{ m/s}^2$.
Net acceleration $= a_c = 8\text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.question: If vector $\vec{A} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$ and vector $\vec{B} = 7\hat{i} + 24\hat{j}$, the vector having the same magnitude as $\vec{B}$ and parallel to $\vec{A}$ is:
questions.solution:
Magnitude of $\vec{B}$: $|\vec{B}| = \sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = \sqrt{49 + 576} = \sqrt{625} = 25$.
Unit vector along $\vec{A}$: $\hat{A} = \frac{3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}}{\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}} = \frac{3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}}{5}$.
Required vector $= |\vec{B}|\hat{A} = 25 \left(\frac{3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}}{5}\right) = 5(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) = 15\hat{i} + 20\hat{j}$.

questions.question: The angle between the two vectors $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{B} = 6\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = (2)(6) + (2)(-3) + (-1)(2) = 12 - 6 - 2 = 4$$
$$|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{4+4+1} = 3, \quad |\vec{B}| = \sqrt{36+9+4} = 7$$
$$\cos\theta = \frac{\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B}}{|\vec{A}||\vec{B}|} = \frac{4}{3 \times 7} = \frac{4}{21} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{21}\right)$$

questions.question: A stone is tied to one end of a string of length $0.5\text{ m}$ and whirled in a horizontal circle with a constant speed. If the stone makes 10 revolutions in $2\pi\text{ seconds}$, its acceleration is:
questions.solution:
Frequency $f = \frac{10}{2\pi}\text{ rev/s} \implies \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \left(\frac{10}{2\pi}\right) = 10\text{ rad/s}$.
$$a = \omega^2 r = (10)^2 \times 0.5 = 100 \times 0.5 = 50\text{ m/s}^2$$

questions.question: What is the projection of vector $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ on vector $\vec{B} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$?

A bomber plane flies horizontally at a height of $500\text{ m}$ with velocity $100\text{ m/s}$. It releases a bomb to hit a target on the ground. At what horizontal distance from the target should the bomb be released? (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
Time to fall: $t = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 500}{10}} = 10\text{ s}$.
Horizontal distance $x = u t = 100 \times 10 = 1000\text{ m}$.

questions.question: Which of the following vectors is perpendicular to $\vec{A} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}$?
questions.solution: Dot product with option (1): $(3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}) \cdot (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) = (3)(2) + (-2)(3) = 6 - 6 = 0$. Hence, it is perpendicular.

questions.question: In uniform circular motion, the angle between velocity vector and acceleration vector at any instant is:
questions.solution: Velocity is tangential to the circular trajectory while centripetal acceleration is directed along the radius towards the centre. The angle between them is always $90^\circ$.

questions.question: The maximum range of a projectile fired with velocity $u$ is $R_{\text{max}}$. The maximum height attained corresponding to this maximum range is:
questions.solution:
Maximum range occurs at $\theta = 45^\circ$, where $R_{\text{max}} = \frac{u^2}{g}$.
Height attained at $\theta = 45^\circ$: $H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2 45^\circ}{2g} = \frac{u^2(1/2)}{2g} = \frac{u^2}{4g} = \frac{R_{\text{max}}}{4}$.

questions.question: Three concurrent forces $\vec{F}_1 = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$, $\vec{F}_2 = -5\hat{i} + \hat{j}$, and $\vec{F}_3$ keep a particle in equilibrium. The force $\vec{F}_3$ is:
questions.solution:
For equilibrium: $\vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2 + \vec{F}_3 = \vec{0}$.
$$\vec{F}_3 = -(\vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2) = -[(2-5)\hat{i} + (3+1)\hat{j}] = -[-3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}] = 3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}$$
